$comment: Atlas governance policy — ADMIN-OWNED BY INTENT, versioned. WARNING, read this before trusting the file: the CODEOWNERS + branch-protection lock described in docs/governance/policy-lock.md is NOT IN FORCE. The previous wording said it COULD NOT be turned on (a 403 under the old private plan); that became false when the repo went public on 2026-08-01, and this comment was stale until 2026-08-02. Measured 2026-08-02: master IS protected (required check 'gate', enforce_admins on, no force-push, no deletion), but the leg that would gate THIS file is off — require_code_owner_reviews is false, required_approving_review_count is 0, and a CODEOWNERS is only now being added. So the lock is ACHIEVABLE and NOT YET CONFIGURED, which is a different claim from the one this comment used to make. Two further preconditions, neither met at the time of writing: the atlas-admins team holds no grant on this repository, and automation currently pushes under the owner's own GitHub identity — a review requirement cannot distinguish two actors sharing one identity. Anyone with write access can therefore still edit this file directly. The ONE control that IS live is the loader's fail-closed default: absent/malformed => empty scopes => NO write is authorized.

nearDup.$comment: Near-duplicate matcher threshold (feeds @atlas/knowledge NearDupConfig.claimNormThreshold). 1 = exact-match only (conservative). Lower toward ~0.85 to merge near-synonym claims once the synonym-tau is trusted.

t0Heuristic.$comment: Keywords that flag a fact as a T0 (human-ratification) candidate.

authz.$comment: Owner-scoped write (KNOW-11): scope => actor ids authorized to write it. Reads are universal regardless. An unlisted scope or actor is fail-closed (no write). THE RULE THIS FILE IS EDITED BY: a scope is listed here only once something actually writes it. Listing a scope GRANTS power; an unlisted one is the safe state, not an omission. `core/knowledge` was removed on 2026-08-02 for exactly that reason — it held a placeholder actor, no production code ever wrote it (its only other occurrences are test fixtures that declare their own policy), and no projection existed. A grant with no user is a standing hole, not a convenience.
authz.$comment-atlas-mined: NOTE THE PLACEMENT: this sits beside `scopes`, never inside it. `scopes` is a Record<string, string[]> and policy.ts:183 returns undefined for ANY entry whose value is not an array of strings — which fail-closes the WHOLE policy to empty scopes, i.e. nobody may write anything. A comment written inside `scopes` would therefore brick governance silently and present as an unexplained `unauthorized`. — Facts MINED by genesis land at scope `atlas:mined` (packages/cli/src/mine.ts). Granting it APPOINTS A CURATOR: it is what lets the promotion door write at all, and without it every promotion is correctly refused `unauthorized`. It is held by the ORCHESTRATOR, not by a human, because this goal runs on the MACHINE path — the explorer proposes and the ratifier promotes, with no human writing a fact. WHAT THIS GRANT DOES AND DOES NOT BUY, so nobody assumes more: it decides WHO MAY WRITE THIS NAMESPACE, not whether a fact is TRUE. Truth is decided by the truth gate, which re-derives every claim against its anchor mechanically and refuses what does not hold, whoever wrote it. And the honest limit: the ratifier's own decision is only `token non-empty` plus `T0 requires billy`, so a T2 fact written by the holder of this scope with a valid token is effectively self-certified — the protection is the grounding gate, not this line.
